description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Abdominal pain history structure
points: Characterize pain with location, onset, character, radiation, timing, exacerbating/relieving factors, severity.
Always screen GI bleed and obstruction red flags early.
Region (RUQ/RLQ/epigastric) narrows the first differential branch.

modules.title: Murphy sign teaching
points: Murphy sign: inspiratory arrest during RUQ palpation suggests gallbladder inflammation.
Positive Murphy + RUQ pain → prioritize biliary ultrasound pathway.
Absence of Murphy does not exclude biliary disease.

modules.title: Peritoneal signs
points: Guarding, rigidity, and rebound suggest peritoneal irritation — treat as acute abdomen until proven otherwise.
Do not delay surgical review for prolonged outpatient workup.
Keep NBM and document serial exams.

modules.title: GI bleeding basics
points: Hematemesis/melena → upper bleed until proven otherwise; hematochezia may be brisk upper or lower.
Resuscitation precedes definitive endoscopy.
Use existing EGD documentation module when endoscopy is performed.

modules.title: Appendicitis pattern
points: RLQ pain + anorexia/nausea/fever is a classic teaching cluster — still confirm with exam/imaging.
Rebound/guarding raise urgency for surgical review.

Q000001.why_ask: Capture the patient's words — it anchors the whole HPI and avoids premature labeling.
Q000001.think: Quote briefly; then structure with SOCRATES/OLDCARTS.

Q000002.why_ask: Time course separates acute abdomen from chronic/recurrent pain.
Q000002.think: Hours + severe → escalate red-flag and surgical thinking early.

Q000003.why_ask: Sudden vs gradual onset changes the first differential branch.
Q000003.think: Sudden severe → perforation, ischemia, colic, rupture on the shortlist.

Q000004.why_ask: Location is the first anatomic filter for abdominal pain.
Q000004.think: Point with one finger if possible; diffuse pain widens the differential.

Q000005.why_ask: Radiation patterns are classic teaching clues (biliary → scapula; pancreatic → back).
Q000005.think: Radiation does not prove a diagnosis — it prioritizes the next questions.

Q000006.why_ask: Character (colicky vs constant vs burning) guides visceral vs peritoneal thinking.
Q000006.think: Colic → hollow viscus spasm/obstruction; constant + guarding → inflammation.

Q000042.why_ask: Region mapping is the fastest way to teach differential branching.

Q000033.why_ask: GI bleed screening is a must-not-miss red flag in every abdominal pain HPI.
Q000033.think: Any bleed + instability → resuscitate first; endoscopy pathway next.

Q000034.why_ask: Vomiting blood vs coffee-ground separates acuity of upper GI bleed.
Q000034.think: Pair with hemodynamic status and melena questions.

Q000035.why_ask: Black stools vs bright red blood redirects upper vs lower bleed thinking.
Q000035.think: Brisk upper bleed can present as hematochezia — do not dismiss.

Q000045.why_ask: Weight loss with pain raises alarm for malignancy, malabsorption, or chronic inflammation.
Q000045.think: Document amount/timeframe; link to red-flag workup later.

Q000021.why_ask: Anorexia + RLQ pain is a classic appendicitis teaching cluster.
Q000021.think: Combine with migration of pain and fever — still confirm on exam.

Q000022.why_ask: Nausea/vomiting accompany many acute abdomen patterns but help urgency triage.

Q000073.why_ask: Syncope/collapse with abdominal pain → bleed, rupture, or sepsis until proven otherwise.
Q000073.think: Stop and escalate — this is a stop-rule mindset question.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: RUQ branch
points: Think biliary colic / cholecystitis / hepatitis / pneumonia referred.
Next history: fatty-food trigger, radiation to scapula, fever, dark urine/jaundice.
Exam later: Murphy sign teaching applies.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: RLQ branch
points: Think appendicitis, mesenteric adenitis, gyn causes, ureteric stone.
Ask anorexia, nausea, fever, migration from periumbilical.
Exam later: rebound / Rovsing / psoas teaching.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: epigastric branch
points: Think peptic ulcer, pancreatitis, gastritis, sometimes ACS referred.
Ask NSAID/alcohol use, radiation to back, vomiting.
Bleed questions remain mandatory even if pain seems ‘ulcer-like’.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: sudden-onset mindset
points: Sudden severe pain → perforation, ischemia, rupture, biliary/renal colic.
Prioritize red flags and exam for peritonitis.
Do not spend the whole interview on chronic background yet.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: GI bleed pathway
points: Resuscitation and risk stratification before detailed chronic history.
Clarify hematemesis vs melena vs hematochezia.
Endoscopy pathway — educational link to your GI module later.
